album: How Visible Cloaks Stitched Themselves Back Together
excerpt: It’s been nine years since Visible Cloaks (the duo of Spencer Doran and Ryan Carlile) released their last studio album, Reassemblage . In the interim, there have been EPs and collaborative records ; Doran also scored the video game Season: A Letter to the Future . But for those of us mesmerized by their previous album, it’s been a long wait to hear a new full-length outing from these master electronic manipulators.

Takkak Takkak make cultural cross-pollination seem easy. Bursting out of the gates with a thunderous mix of metal, electronica, and traditional Japanese and Indonesian sonics, Shigeru Ishihara and Johanes “Mo’ong” Santoso Pribadi grab the reins of their various wild elements and boldly steer them across a landscape of their own design.

album: Lea Bertucci and Norbert Rodenkirchen Reanimate Early Music
excerpt: For more than a decade the music of reedist, composer, and improviser Lea Bertucci has revealed a broad scope, an evolving body of work that explores meditation, freedom, history, and language in ever-shifting ways. Her innate curiosity and restlessness have been fed by a host of disparate projects, both solo endeavors and collaborative works with the likes of Olivia Block , Amirtha Kidambi , Ben Vida , and Lawrence English , among others.
